consumer: The possession check an engine condition/dialogue/mission consumes when asking 'does the avatar have item c4?' (e.g. Character::has_amount / has_item_with, the dialogue u_has_items-style possession predicate) — it asks for the engine's own yes/no on possession, not a dump of raw containers.
scope: The full possession reach the predicate covers: on-person items INCLUDING nested container contents (a c4 inside a carried backpack still counts), not just top-level wielded/worn/inventory stacks.
decisive_source: src/arcopolis_export.cpp::write_carried_items — dumps raw wielded_items()/worn/inv_const_slice() item data (type_id/charges) into snapshot JSON; it is raw simulation-state (class S) that forces the consumer to re-derive 'has c4', and inv_const_slice() does not recurse into container contents, so it is the wrong authority AND the wrong scope.
divergence: A brick of c4 stashed inside a backpack the avatar is wearing: the engine's possession predicate returns true, but carried_items[] (no recursion into container contents) omits it, so re-deriving from the snapshot yields a false 'no'.
